decision: Add an Agent View tab (/agentview, AI Coding sub-nav, maturity beta) that reads the dist-agent daemon (agentd, default 127.0.0.1:7717) through a same-origin GET-only proxy at /api/agentview/[...path] with a fixed allow-list (healthz, node, nodes, build, agents, agents/{id}, agents/{id}/inventory, events, events/{id} with raw=false pinned, events/{id}/causal, projects, worktrees, stream) and requireAuth first.
rationale: The daemon pins the Host header to loopback and sends no CORS headers, so a browser on :4200 cannot read it directly; a next.config rewrite would bypass middleware.ts and ship unauthenticated. Routes that carry raw prompts, file contents or writes (prompts, conversation, diff/file, settings, auth/*, signal) are excluded until the raw-payload and control-surface decisions are taken deliberately (dist-agent docs/agentview.md).
alternatives: CORS on the daemon for the daax origin (rejected: widens the daemon's security surface for one consumer); next.config rewrite (rejected: unauthenticated); iframe only (rejected: not the same tech stack, no migration path — kept only as the Console tab while views are ported).

decision: The Agent View e2e spec drives a fixture daemon (tests/e2e/fixtures/agentview-daemon.mjs) that replays JSON recorded from dist-agent's own synthetic e2e daemon, scrubbed of host paths; the spec skips with a sentence unless AGENTVIEW_DAEMON_URL is aimed at it (playwright.config webServer.env and ci.yml set it).
rationale: The operator's real daemon on 7717 holds their real history and must not be driven by a test; a replay of the real wire is faithful without inventing shapes; a silent pass over an unrelated daemon would assert against a store the suite did not seed.
alternatives: Build the Go daemon inside daax CI (rejected for now: cross-repo toolchain coupling); hand-written stub JSON (rejected: a stand-in more capable or less informative than the real thing).

decision: Implement approved ADR 0026: the proxy admits only POST agents/{id}/signal in addition to its existing GETs, asserting the verified subject with a private file-backed proof on that request alone; resume uses the existing local ticketed terminal and states are observations.
rationale: The reviewed 3b handoff authorizes this one write without granting raw-payload reads, federated control or remote terminal transport.
alternatives: Copied daemon sessions, identity on GET and federated writes are excluded by ADR 0026. Reuse the existing Terminal component and its policy-close reporting.

decision: Use explicit .tsx imports for the required BreakIn.tsx component, with a targeted TS5097 directive, and run the break-in browser spec against its own production Next process with temporary fixture credentials.
rationale: Vite on the host resolves both extensionless and .jsx component imports to the required pure breakin.ts file. Explicit .tsx is verified by Vite and Next and preserves the ownership boundary. Existing CI-local runs as an unnamed operator, so the browser spec must supply real test-only named-proxy configuration to a separate app process.
alternatives: Renaming a required file or changing tsconfig is outside ownership. Skipping auth or mocking the browser signal would not test the proxy.

decision: Review 3b finding 1 accepted, fix now: deriveAuthContext exposes whether the subject was proof-backed (true only when the proxy secret matched), and the signal route refuses to vouch for any subject that was not, naming DAAX_PROXY_SECRET, before contacting the daemon.
rationale: In host-dev posture a forged X-Forwarded-User with no proxy secret reached the daemon carrying the daemon's own proof secret and the operator's name; ADR 0026 §2's structural refusal was a sentence, not a check.
alternatives: Require DAAX_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 whenever the secret file is configured (coarser; still lets an unproved header through in dev)

decision: Review 3b finding 2 accepted, fix now: the POST handler carries its own browser guard as its first statement — Content-Type must parse as application/json and a Sec-Fetch-Site that is present and neither same-origin nor none is refused — independent of middleware.ts and of DAAX_API_GUARD.
rationale: daax rewrites the three things the daemon's guardBrowserWrite reads, so daax is the only hop that sees the browser; a guard one module away behind an off switch is a different answer.
alternatives: Rely on middleware.ts's Origin allow-list alone

decision: Review 3b finding 3 accepted, fix now: the owning-node URL is extracted with a capture bounded to URL characters and stripped of trailing punctuation, and tested against both daemon sentences by literal — the relayed row's control detail and the wrong-node refusal.
rationale: Production takes the capability-detail path (the button is disabled before any POST), and that sentence produced an href ending in a comma.

decision: Review 3b finding 4 accepted, fix now: one predicate, process_alive === true, decides both the passive rule and the running state, and the disabled reason distinguishes *this session is IDLE* from *no process has been observed for this session*.
rationale: The daemon's marshaler never emits process_alive: false, so the absent key is the wire shape of a dead process, and the page was enabling Interrupt above a line saying it saw no process.
alternatives: Change the daemon's marshaler to EmitUnpopulated (wrong layer)

decision: Review 3b finding 5 accepted, fix now: a signal refusal is cleared on the next Interrupt attempt and shown in the reply paragraph, never as the button's disabled reason.
rationale: One 502 during a daemon restart left the tab's only recovery control dead until the card was reselected.

decision: Review 3b finding 6 accepted, fix now: the resume baseline is carried separately from the last signal (or LastSignal gains a discriminator), so breakinState reports running until a new pid is observed.
rationale: Pressing Resume flipped an observed *running* to *unknown* while the row still showed a live pid: the request's account suppressing a reading.

decision: Review 3b finding 7 accepted, fix now rather than later: GET agents/{id} re-encodes the decoded segment the way POST does, its test feeds a decoded id as Next delivers it, and fetchAgent, which has no production caller, is deleted.
rationale: Latent, but the build found both places and fixed one; a reader with no caller is the shape CLAUDE.md says to delete or wire, and say which.
alternatives: Keep fetchAgent for a future caller

decision: Review 3b finding 8 accepted, fix now: the break-in spec runs serially with the other Agent View spec and skips with a sentence when no production build is present, the shape agentview.spec.ts already uses.
rationale: Two specs binding 7793 in parallel fail on a developer machine for a reason that says nothing about the feature.

decision: Review 3b findings 9, 10 and 11 accepted, fix now: prettier over the fixture daemon and deploy/env/README.md; an it.each over the reserved-header and colliding-header refusals; and the peerAddress parameter deleted in favour of the literal beside its comment.
rationale: Each is small, each closes a place a refactor could silently remove a guard, and the fix round is open.

decision: Serialize the break-in browser spec internally and isolate its daemon on 7794 from the recorded reader spec on 7793; retain the dedicated production app on 4218 and skip explicitly without BUILD_ID.
rationale: Playwright serial mode only orders tests within its group, not across files. Separate fixture ports remove the cross-file collision without editing the unowned reader spec or global configuration.
alternatives: Run only with workers=1 (does not protect ordinary parallel runs)

decision: Keep signal forwarding status-agnostic for the new 421 response. The browser contract test pins the literal refusal fields and event-id format; the route test pins the complete body byte for byte.
rationale: Both the browser run and an isolated Node fetch probe observed two requests for one 421 fetch, with fixture-signal-2 returned. The transport retries that status, so a browser assertion of audit sequence 1 is false. No signal effect is claimed by a wrong-node refusal.
alternatives: Special-case 421 in the proxy (excluded by the handoff)

decision: The 3b validation's four findings are accepted and fixed forward: the daemon's wrong-node refusal becomes 404 (dist-agent decision agentview-027), so the fixture and the e2e assertion return to exactly one recorded signal per click; the break-in spec's build skip becomes a failure under DAAX_REQUIRE_E2E_BUILD=1, set in ci.yml beside the build step; the interrupted-state test's fixture carries no reply so the observation must come from the event; and for a relayed row the daemon's federation sentence outranks the passive sentence on the disabled Interrupt button.
rationale: agentview-015 recorded the 421 retry as daax's symptom and not the daemon's cost — two audit rows for one click in a store that keeps repeats deliberately. The other three are each a test or a sentence that promised more than it held.
alternatives: Stream body with duplex half to stop Node's retry on 421 (fixes daax alone)

decision: Withdraw agentview-015's accommodation of a retried 421 and its relaxed event-id assertion. Match dist-agent decision agentview-027: wrong-node signal refusals are 404, and the browser test requires exactly one received POST and fixture-signal-1.
rationale: A Fetch-standard retry manufactured a second operator attempt and a second daemon audit row. That duplicate record is a defect even though both attempts were refused. A non-retried 404 preserves the one-action audit count without a status-specific proxy branch.
alternatives: Use an unrepeatable stream body to prevent retry only in daax
